source.title: Recent developments and open problems in linear series

accepted.question_text: Let S = {p1, ..., pr} be distinct points in projective space P^N over an algebraically closed field, let X be the blow-up of P^N at those points, and let L(d,m)=dH-m(E1+...+Er). Waldschmidt defined e(S)=lim_{m→∞} a(S,m)/m, where a(S,m) is the least degree d for which h^0(X,L(d,m))>0. Develop computational or conceptual methods for evaluating, estimating, or bounding the Waldschmidt constant e(S).
accepted.context_brief: Waldschmidt constants for blown-up projective space

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1.1 Develop computational or conceptual methods for evaluating, esti�mating or bounding e(S).

accepted.question_text: Let S be a finite set of points in P^N. Suppose there exists m such that a(S,m)/m = (a(S,1)+N-1)/N, where a(S,m) is the least degree of a divisor vanishing to order at least m on S. Must S then either lie in a hyperplane or be a star configuration? More generally, if the Waldschmidt constant satisfies e(S) = (a(S,1)+N-1)/N, must the same conclusion hold?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1.3 If for some m we have a(S, m)/m = (a(S, 1) + N - 1)/N is it true that S is either contained in a hyperplane or is a star configuration? What if e(S) = (a(S, 1) + N - 1)/N?

accepted.question_text: Let X be the blow-up of P^N at distinct points p1, ..., pr, and let D = dH - m1E1 - ... - mrEr. Is there a general method to determine whether D is semi-effective, meaning that h^0(X,nD)>0 for some integer n>0?
accepted.context_brief: Semi-effectivity on blow-ups of projective space

evidence.quote: Definition 2.2.1 Let X be an algebraic variety and L a line bundle on X. We say that L is semi-effective, if there exists n > 0 such that h0(nL) > 0. ... Problem 2.2.2 Is there a way to determine if D is semi-effective?

accepted.question_text: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at points p1, ..., pr, and let D = dH - m1E1 - ... - mrEr. Assume that D is special, meaning that D is effective and h^1(X,D)>0. Must every positive multiple nD with n>1 also be special?

evidence.quote: Assume that the divisor D is special (i.e., D is effective with h1(X, D) > 0). Is it then true that nD is special for all n > 1?

accepted.question_text: For a monomial ideal I ⊂ k[x,y], let Z = Spec(k[x,y]/I), and let Hilb^I_S denote the irreducible constructible subset of Hilb^n(S) parametrizing subschemes of a smooth projective surface S that are isomorphic to Z. Describe Hilb^I_S: is it locally closed, and what adjacency relations occur among these loci inside the Hilbert scheme?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4.1 Describe HilbIS. Is it locally closed? What adjacencies are there between such subsets of the Hilbert scheme?

accepted.question_text: With the same notation, let Y be a general subscheme of a smooth projective surface S corresponding to a monomial ideal I, and let D be a divisor on S. Find conditions on S, I, and D that determine or constrain the cohomology of I_Y ⊗ O_S(D), ideally giving criteria that force h^0(I_Y ⊗ O_S(D)) = max{0, h^0(O_S(D)) - n}.
accepted.context_brief: Cohomology of monomial subschemes on surfaces

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4.2 What can we say (or conjecture) about the cohomology of IY ⊗ OS(D)? To be more precise, it would be nice to have conditions on S, I and D implying that h0 = max{0, h0(OS(D)) - n}.

accepted.question_text: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at generic points p1, ..., ps. The SHGH conjecture predicts that every prime divisor C on X satisfies h^1(X,O_X(C))=0. How can this conjectural vanishing statement be extended after removing the assumption that the blown-up points are generic?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.5.1 (SHGH) Let C ⊂ X be a prime divisor where X → P2 is the blow-up of generic points p1, . . . , ps. Then h1(X, OX(C)) = 0. Problem 2.5.2 How can we remove the assumption about the points being generic in the SHGH Conjecture?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a projective manifold with large algebraic fundamental group and let L be an ample line bundle on X. Given a positive number N, does there exist a finite étale cover p: X'→X such that either (1) the Seshadri number of p^*L at every point of X' is greater than N, or (2) the Seshadri number of p_e^*(p_1^*L \otimes p_2^*L) along the diagonal in X'	imes X' is greater than N? If not in general, what condition on the fundamental group of X guarantees such a positive answer?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.6.2 Let X be a projective manifold with large algebraic fundamental group and let L be an ample line bundle on X. (1) Given a positive number N, does there exist a finite étale cover p : X' → X such that the Seshadri number of p∗L at any point is bigger than N? (2) ... along D' is bigger than N? (3) If the answer to (1) or (2) is negative or unclear, what is the condition on the fundamental group of X to guarantee a positive answer?

accepted.question_text: For a hyperplane arrangement A in P^n, let C(A) denote the Orlik-Terao algebra. Do the results known for line arrangements in P^2 extend to higher dimension? In particular, can one give an explicit description of the graded Betti numbers of C(A) in terms of the geometry of A?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7.2 Do the results for lines in P2 generalize to higher dimension? For example, if A ⊆ Pn, then [45] shows that the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of C(A) is bounded by n. Can an explicit description of the graded betti numbers of C(A) be given in terms of the geometry of A?

accepted.question_text: Let (R,m) be a regular local ring of dimension n and let I⊂R be an ideal of big height e. Determine whether the strengthened symbolic-power containments listed in Problem 2.8.2 hold, namely whether I^(m) is contained in m^{rn-r}I^r for m≥rn, in m^{rn-r-(n-1)}I^r for m≥ rn-(n-1), in m^{re-r}I^r for m≥re, and in m^{re-r-(e-1)}I^r for m≥ re-(e-1).

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8.2 Suppose (R, m) is a regular local ring of dimension n and I ⊆ R is an ideal with bight(I) = e. Then do the following hold? 1. I(m) ⊆ mrn−r Ir for m ≥ rn. 2. I(m) ⊆ mrn−r−(n−1)Ir for m ≥ rn − (n − 1). 3. I(m) ⊆ mre−r Ir for m ≥ re. 4. I(m) ⊆ mre−r−(e−1)Ir for m ≥ re − (e − 1).

accepted.question_text: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at r distinct points in arbitrary position, and let L be an effective nef divisor on X. Must one of the following happen: (a) there exists m>1 such that h^1(X,mL)=0, with m=1 expected when the points are in general position; or (b) there exists a possibly reducible curve C on X with |L-C| nonempty, arithmetic genus p_a(C)>0, and intersection number L·C=0?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2.4 Let X be the blow-up of P2 at r distinct points ... and let L be an effective nef divisor on X. Then is it true that either a) there exists m > 1 such that h1(mL) = 0 ... or b) there is a (not necessarily irreducible) curve C on X such that |L − C| ≠ ∅, pa(C) > 0 and L · C = 0?

accepted.question_text: Let f:Y→B be a morphism from a smooth projective threefold to a smooth curve whose general fiber is a smooth surface. Fix an integer g>0. Is there a constant b(Y,g) such that every vertical curve C contained in a fiber, with geometric genus g, satisfies C^2 ≥ -b(Y,g), where self-intersection is computed inside the fiber containing C?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3.6 Let f : Y → B be a morphism from a smooth projective threefold Y to a smooth curve B such that the general fibre is a smooth surface. Is there a constant b(Y, g) such that C2 ≥ −b(Y, g) for all vertical curves C ⊂ Y ... of geometric genus g?

accepted.question_text: For a smooth projective surface X, is the global Seshadri constant ε(X)=inf{ε(L): L in Pic(X) ample} always positive?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.6.1 Is the global Seshadri constant ε(X) := inf {ε(L) L ∈ Pic(X) ample} positive for every smooth projective surface X?

accepted.question_text: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at r general points, let D be an effective divisor on X, and let E be a (-1)-curve. For the restriction map from the complete linear system |D| to |D|_E|, must all base points in the image come from a fixed base curve of |D|, and, if |D| has no fixed component, must the restriction map have maximal rank?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.9.3 Let X be the blow-up of P2 in r general points, D an effective divisor on X and E a (−1)-curve. For the restriction map |D| ρ→ |D|E| one has: 1. All base points in the image of ρ come from a base curve in |D|. 2. If |D| has no fixed component, then ρ has maximal rank.

accepted.question_text: Fix integers d,m1,...,mn, and consider plane curves of degree d with multiplicities m1,...,mn at n points, where the first r points are collinear and the remaining points are otherwise general. Is it true that if d > m1 + ... + mr, then nonemptiness of the linear system for n general points is equivalent to nonemptiness of the corresponding linear system when the first r points are constrained to be collinear?
accepted.context_brief: Linear systems with some collinear base points

evidence.quote: Problem 3.9.4 Is it true that, if d > m1 + · · · + mr, then L(d; m1, . . . , mn) ≠ ∅ if and only if L(d; m1, . . . , mr, mr+1, . . . , mn) ≠ ∅?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. Does there exist a constant b(X) such that every reduced irreducible curve C on X satisfies C^2 ≥ -b(X)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3.1 (Bounded Negativity) Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. There exists a positive constant b(X) bounding the self-intersection of reduced, irreducible curves on X.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero and let g>0. Does there exist a constant b(X,g) such that every reduced irreducible curve of geometric genus g on X satisfies C^2 ≥ -b(X,g)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3.4 (Weak Bounded Negativity) Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero and let g > 0 be an integer. There exists a positive constant b(X, g) bounding the self-intersection of curves of geometric genus g on X.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero and let g>0. Does there exist a constant b_s(X,g) such that every smooth irreducible curve of geometric genus g on X satisfies C^2 ≥ -b_s(X,g)?
accepted.context_brief: Very weak bounded negativity for smooth curves

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3.5 (Very Weak Bounded Negativity) Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero and let g > 0 be an integer. There exists a positive constant bs(X, g) bounding the self-intersection of smooth curves of geometric genus g.
